title: The Drop of Tashkent
premise: Ines Oyelaran, a Tashkent-based interpreter for a faltering peace delegation, receives a calendar invitation from a handler who died three days ago — scheduled for tomorrow, at a checkpoint café that doesn't officially exist. The invitation is a trap set by the covert network that trained Ines years ago, now tying off loose ends before the delegation's collapse triggers an international audit. To survive the night and expose the network's role in the 'incident' that broke their sleep, Ines must play the loyal asset one last time, feeding the network false confirmation while smuggling evidence to a delegation rival they were ordered to distrust. At dawn, as the checkpoint shifts change, Ines burns the network's ledger publicly, choosing truth — and a self they've never been allowed to be — over the only belonging they've ever known.
about_author: Orsen Okafor is the pen name of a former conference interpreter who spent a decade working high-stakes diplomatic summits across Central Asia and West Africa before turning to fiction. They write thrillers about people who live in the space between languages, where every translation is a small act of betrayal.

chapters.title: The Invitation from a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, three sleepless days after the 'incident' at the delegation's hotel. A calendar ping arrives from handler Marek Voss — dead since Tuesday — summoning them to a checkpoint café at 05:40, minutes before the border shift change. Ines recognizes the phrasing of the invitation as a training code: a loyalty test. The beat is dread sharpening into cold clarity; Ines decides to attend, but not alone.

chapters.title: Coffee at the Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Ines arrives at the café and finds not Voss's killers but Voss himself, alive, faking his death to force the network's hand — and he names Ines as the incident's designated scapegoat. Alternating with the POV of Deputy Delegate Amara Sefu, whom Ines secretly tips off. The beat is vertigo: the one person Ines trusted is the trap, and the stranger is the lifeline.

chapters.title: Every Word a Weapon
chapters.summary: Climax. Ines interprets the delegation's final session while running a double channel: feeding the network's listening post a doctored translation that incriminates its own director, while Amara extracts Voss's ledger from the hotel safe. The network realizes mid-session and moves to take Ines at the checkpoint. The beat is controlled fury — Ines weaponizes the very skill that once made them obedient.

chapters.title: Shift Change
chapters.summary: Ines's POV at 05:40. As the border guards rotate, Ines stands at the checkpoint, ledger transmitted, network exposed, Voss in custody, and the delegation collapsing exactly as predicted — but with the truth now on the record. Ines crosses the border not as an asset, a scapegoat, or an interpreter-for-hire, but as a witness. The beat is exhausted, hard-won belonging to oneself at last.
